name: 211info Announces New Statewide Emergency Management Director - 211info
description: New role will equip referral and information service to provide coordinated response during emergency events PORTLAND, Ore., February 2, 2022 – 211info announced today a newly created role that will position the referral and information service to more efficiently respond to statewide emergencies. Kerry Hoeschen, who has been with the nonprofit for almost two years and served most recently as 211info’s COVID-19 Program Manager, will step into the position of Statewide Emergency Management Director. In this role, Hoeschen will lead 211info’s emergency planning, processes and partnerships to support people throughout Oregon. “Between COVID-19 and the climate crisis, we’re starting to see years with multiple emergencies: extreme weather events, wildfires and the ripple effects of two years of living through a pandemic have taken a toll,” explained Dan Herman, 211info’s Chief Executive Officer. “This new role will enable Kerry and her team to create more structure to streamline our organization’s response.” Hoeschen will lead 211info’s emergency management team and provide leadership to 211info’s community engagement coordinators, working closely with local, regional and state emergenc

name: 211info Announces Reduction in Phone Service Hours Due to Funding Cuts - 211info
description: Updated: July 2, 2025 4:40pm PORTLAND, Ore., July 1, 2025 — 211info, the private nonprofit that manages the 211 system for Oregon and Southwest Washington, announced today that it will reduce its core phone service hours after July 4, 2025. Regular phone hours will shift from 24/7 operations, to Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 6 PM, due to funding reductions. “We know this change may create additional barriers for people seeking help,” said Dan Herman, CEO of 211info. “This is not the level of service our community deserves, and we believe everyone should have easy, reliable access to critical resources. Unfortunately, reduced funding means we are unable to maintain 24/7 phone service at this time.” 211info remains fully functional during its new core operating hours, providing information and referral services for housing, food, child care, health care, utility assistance, and other essential needs. In addition, community members can text their zip code to 898211 or email [email protected] , and 211info will follow up during open hours. A searchable online database is available at 211info.org. description: Calling 211 is the fastest way to find local clean air spaces and cooling centers. Our specially trained teams ensure our database is timely and accurate, and that a live person helps each caller. Phone interpretation is available in over 240 languages. How Calling 211 Can Help During Extreme Heat & Wildfires As a nonprofit contact center, 211info serves as the “front desk” for agencies to help relay important information like shelter and center locations, hours, and availability during emergencies. We can also help coordinate transportation using available local options, as directed by local agencies. DURING DISASTER OR EMERGENCY During declared emergencies, 211info partners with the Oregon Office of Resilience and Emergency Management and multiple local agencies to coordinate additional services as they become available. name: Southwest Washington 211 Services Now Managed by WA 211 - 211info
description: As of January 1, 2026, 211info serves all 36 counties in Oregon, and Washington 211 (WA 211) serves communities in Southwest Washington. This change reflects WA 211’s transition from multiple regional 211 offices to a centralized, statewide hub. Oregon already operates under a similar model, with a single point of coordination statewide. 211info previously managed 211 services in Clark and Skamania counties beginning in 2004, and in Cowlitz and Wahkiakum counties beginning in 2015. With Washington’s new hub model, WA 211 now serves these counties directly. What this means for people calling 211 For individuals and families, nothing changes. Calling 211 still connects you to resources in your community. Calls are automatically routed to the appropriate local 211, based on where you are calling from. name: Fresh Food & Real Help: How 211info and the Farm Direct Nutrition Program Support Older Adults - 211info
description: Food insecurity is a growing concern for many as prices continue to climb. But for older adults on fixed incomes, even basics like fresh, healthy food can feel out of reach. That’s where the Senior Farm Direct Nutrition Program (SFDNP) can help. SFDNP provides eligible seniors with vouchers to buy locally grown fruits, vegetables, and herbs from participating farmers’ markets and farm stands from June through November. The program not only helps older adults stretch their food budgets, but it also supports local farmers and strengthens our community food system. Research shows that programs like SFDNP have played a key role in creating and sustaining farmers’ markets in underserved communities, increasing access to fresh produce for everyone. Get Personalized Assistance 211info partners with the Oregon Health Authority to operate the Senior Farm Direct Helpline from April 1 to November 30 (program starts April 1, vouchers available for use June 1), Monday through Friday, 8 am-5 pm. name: COLD RELATED ILLNESS FAQ
description: INFORMATIONAL RECORD COLD RELATED ILLNESS FAQ Print & Share X Print & Share Print PDF It is important to understand the difference between hypothermia and frostbite. Hypothermia is typically a more serious medical condition that always requires emergency medical attention, while frostbite (injury from freezing) should be treated by a medical professional but usually does not warrant emergency action. Severe frostbite, however, can lead to amputation. If you are interested in partnering with 211info, please email [email protected] or reach out to a coordinator from the list of contacts below. If you are in need of community resources, please call 211, Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 6 PM. Some special programs, including Child Care Referrals , Pesticide Reporting, and Resource/Foster Care Support have extended hours. During emergency incidents, 211info may expand operations beyond core hours at the request of state or local officials. When extended hours are implemented, 211info will provide updates on its website and social media.
